app.title: Active Units (Unit Activity Filter)
app.summary: The person points a launcher at spike-sorting output, a table of trial onset times and a set of time-window parameters, and the tool computes each unit's baseline and response firing rate per experiment from a random sample of trials. In the dashboard they choose which experiments the filters apply to, set ranges on baseline rate, response rate, difference, absolute difference and a p-value threshold, and apply them. Per-experiment histograms show the distribution that remains with the cut-offs drawn in, and a count shows how many units pass. They read the passing units in a table and click one to see its spike rasters in every experiment. They can save the thresholds as a rules file and load them again, and they export the list of passing units as a CSV.

task.text: Decide which spike-sorted units to keep for analysis by setting thresholds on their trial-based baseline and stimulus-response firing rates, checking single units against their rasters, and exporting the list that passes.

data.text: Spike times and cluster IDs from a spike sorter, trial onset samples grouped by experiment, and a computed table of baseline and response firing-rate statistics for each unit in each experiment
data.item: a sorted unit (neuron cluster), with its firing-rate statistics in each experiment

stage.text: cleaning a sorted unit set after spike sorting and curation, before response analysis

mechanism.text: Range sliders and experiment checkboxes drive one filter that keeps a unit only if it passes every threshold in every checked experiment. The filter redraws a grid of per-experiment histograms with the cut-offs marked, a passing-count summary and a table of passing units. Selecting a row in the table opens per-experiment spike rasters for that unit.

field.text: trial-based firing-rate filtering of spike-sorted units in extracellular electrophysiology

workflow.name: filter a collection by thresholds on computed measures and export the items that pass

steps.here: A launcher takes the sorted-spikes folder, the trials CSV, an output folder and the window parameters. It then computes the activity summary and opens the dashboard.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For a random sample of trials per experiment, it computes mean and SD firing rates in a baseline window and a response window, their difference, and a paired t-test p-value.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Checkboxes under 'Apply filters to' pick the experiments, and range sliders set baseline, response, difference and absolute difference. A discrete slider sets the p-value cut-off. Apply Filters reruns the filter and updates the passing count.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: A grid of histograms, one column per experiment and one row per metric, shows the units that remain, with dashed red lines at the slider limits.
The table lists the passing units, averaged over the experiments ticked under 'Show in table'. Clicking a row draws that unit's spike rasters around stimulus onset, one panel per experiment.
Save Rules writes the slider ranges to a rules CSV, with open-ended limits stored as infinity. Load Rules reads them back onto the sliders.
Export Units writes the passing unit IDs to a CSV at a chosen path and filename.

distinctive: A unit passes only if it passes every threshold in every checked experiment. Unchecked experiments let it through, so the person can filter on the one experiment that matters most.
Firing rates are estimated from a small random sample of trials in a baseline and a response window set relative to stimulus onset. A paired t-test compares the two windows.
The p-value filter uses fixed significance levels on a discrete slider rather than a continuous range.
Spike rasters for a selected unit are loaded from the raw spike times only on the first click, and they show a random subset of trials in each experiment with the stimulus marked.
